# ScholarFolio

> Free, open source citation metrics dashboard and academic portfolio for
> researchers. Turns a public Google Scholar profile into one page with citation
> trends, a co-author network, h-index, i10-index and field-normalized metrics.

- Data: public Google Scholar profiles, enriched with OpenAlex and Semantic
  Scholar. Profiles are cached and refreshed regularly, so figures are snapshots.
- Claiming: researchers verify ownership through ORCID and get a permanent URL.
- Licence: MIT. Source code: https://github.com/jheller1212/ScholarFolio

## Pages

- [Home](https://scholarfolio.org/): what ScholarFolio is, and profile search.
- [Researcher profile](https://scholarfolio.org/jonas-heller): example of a claimed profile at its vanity URL. Unclaimed profiles live at /scholar/<Google Scholar user ID>. Readable as text for search and answer engines when the profile is cached.
- [About](https://scholarfolio.org/about): data sources, funding and the project behind ScholarFolio.
- [For institutions](https://scholarfolio.org/institutions): sustaining membership.

## Guides

<!-- guides:start (generated by scripts/guides/build.mjs) -->
- [Narrative CV guides](https://scholarfolio.org/guides/): index of all guides below.
- [How to write a narrative CV for a research grant](https://scholarfolio.org/guides/how-to-write-a-narrative-cv/): What narrative CVs have in common across funders, a side-by-side comparison, and a writing method.
- [NWO Veni, Vidi, Vici narrative CV: how to write the evidence-based CV](https://scholarfolio.org/guides/nwo-veni-vidi-vici-narrative-cv/): Academic profile, 10 key outputs, word limits per instrument, and the full list of banned indicators.
- [ERC CV and Track Record: how to write the 4-page section](https://scholarfolio.org/guides/erc-cv-track-record/): Up to four pages, three sections, up to ten research outputs with a short explanation of each.
- [MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship CV: how to write section 4 of Part B-2](https://scholarfolio.org/guides/msca-postdoctoral-fellowship-cv/): Indicative length 5 pages, exact dates, and outputs described by their significance rather than by impact factor.
- [UKRI Résumé for Research and Innovation (R4RI): how to write the narrative CV](https://scholarfolio.org/guides/ukri-r4ri-narrative-cv/): Four modules plus optional context, one résumé for the whole team, word count set by each funding opportunity.
- [SNSF CV format: how to write your major achievements](https://scholarfolio.org/guides/snsf-cv-format/): Five elements, 1–3 narrative achievements, up to 10 selected works, and no proxy metrics.
- [DFG CV template (form 53.200): how to fill it in](https://scholarfolio.org/guides/dfg-cv-template/): Mandatory for all DFG programmes: four pages, up to 10 + 10 publications with a note on your role.
- [Why Google Scholar and OpenAlex citation counts differ](https://scholarfolio.org/guides/google-scholar-vs-openalex-citation-counts/): Different indexes, different matching, different author profiles: what that means for your numbers.
